description: Full port of the OpenTabs Retool plugin: read and write apps (pages), app state and components, folders, resources and resource folders, workflows, runs, triggers and releases, environments, source-control branches and settings, playground queries (run SQL and gRPC), Retool Database grids and AI agents on retool.com in your current tab. Uses your own logged-in Retool session: same-origin /api calls carrying the page's xsrfToken cookie as X-Xsrf-Token.

tools.name: get_current_user
tools.description: Get the profile of the currently authenticated Retool user, including email, name, organization, and account details.

tools.name: change_user_name
tools.description: Update the first and last name of the currently authenticated user.

tools.name: get_organization
tools.description: Get detailed information about the current Retool organization, including name, subdomain, plan, and settings.

tools.name: list_user_spaces
tools.description: List all spaces (workspaces) accessible to the current user. Spaces represent separate Retool organizations or child organizations.

tools.name: list_experiments
tools.description: List all active feature experiments and their values for the current Retool organization. Experiments control feature flags and A/B tests.

tools.name: list_apps
tools.description: List all apps (pages) and folders in the Retool organization. Returns both apps and their folder structure. Apps include web apps, mobile apps, modules, and forms.

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: Get a Retool application by UUID. Returns the page save record including serialized app state, change history, and metadata. For a human-readable lookup by path, use lookup_app instead.

tools.name: get_app_state
tools.description: Get the current app state (Transit-encoded JSON) for a Retool app. Returns the serialized component tree including all widgets, queries, and layout. Use this to read an app before modifying it with save_page. The app_state field is the Transit JSON string that can be parsed, modified, and saved back.

tools.name: lookup_app
tools.description: Look up a Retool application by its URL path (e.g., "fraud/fraud"). Returns the full app state including components, queries, and configuration. Use this when you know the app path but not its UUID.

tools.name: get_app_docs
tools.description: Get the documentation and usage notes for a Retool application. Returns the editor-written description that explains the app purpose and usage.

tools.name: list_app_tags
tools.description: List published version tags (releases) for a Retool application. Tags are named snapshots deployed to end users.

tools.name: list_page_names
tools.description: Get a lightweight list of all app names and UUIDs. Faster and smaller than list_apps — use this when you only need names and UUIDs, not full metadata.

tools.name: list_page_saves
tools.description: List the edit history (saved versions) for a Retool app. Shows who made each save and when. Useful for auditing changes and understanding who last modified an app.

tools.name: list_components
tools.description: List all components (widgets, queries, frames) in a Retool app. Parses the Transit-encoded app state and returns a human-readable list with component IDs, types, positions, and key properties.

tools.name: create_app
tools.description: Create a new Retool web app (page). The app is created in the specified folder. Returns the initial save record.

tools.name: export_toolscript_archive
tools.description: Export a Retool app as a Toolscript ZIP archive using Retool's own browser-side archive serializer. Returns the ZIP as base64 so callers can save, unzip, edit, and later pass it to create_app_from_toolscript_archive or update_app_from_toolscript_archive. Optionally also starts a normal browser download.

tools.name: create_app_from_toolscript_archive
tools.description: Create a new Retool app from a base64-encoded Toolscript ZIP archive. The tool uses Retool's own browser-side Toolscript compiler to turn the ZIP into a Transit appState string, then calls Retool's create page API. The archive determines whether the result is a web app, mobile app, or module.

tools.name: update_app_from_toolscript_archive
tools.description: Overwrite an existing Retool app with a base64-encoded Toolscript ZIP archive. The tool uses Retool's own browser-side Toolscript compiler to produce a Transit appState string, fetches the latest page save ID for optimistic locking, then calls Retool's save API. The target app type must match the archive type when Retool exposes type metadata.

tools.name: force_editor_save
tools.description: Trigger Retool's own editor save pipeline for the currently targeted editor tab. Use this after a Toolscript import or backend app-state update has been loaded in the editor and you need Retool to reconcile editor-only/server-side state without making a manual dummy edit. Requires targeting an open editor tab for the requested page UUID with tabId.

tools.name: clone_app
tools.description: Clone an existing Retool app (page) to create a copy with a new name. The clone is placed in the specified folder.

tools.name: save_page
tools.description: Save (update) a Retool app by pushing its full app state JSON. This is the core tool for programmatically building and modifying Retool apps. The appState must be a valid Transit-encoded JSON string (the same format returned by get_app). Use get_app_state to get the current state, modify it, then use this tool to save changes.

tools.name: add_component
tools.description: Add a UI widget component to a Retool app. Handles Transit JSON manipulation internally — you only need to specify the component type, properties, and position. Common types: TextWidget (markdown text), ButtonWidget2 (button), TextInputWidget (input field), TableWidget2 (data table), SelectWidget (dropdown), NumberInputWidget (number input), CheckboxWidget (checkbox), ContainerWidget (container/frame).

tools.name: add_query
tools.description: Add a data query to a Retool app. The query connects to an existing resource (database, REST API, gRPC service) and can be referenced by widgets via {{ queryName.data }}. For SQL queries, provide the SQL string. For REST queries, provide httpMethod and query (URL path).

tools.name: delete_app
tools.description: Delete (trash) a Retool app by UUID. The app is moved to the trash folder and can be recovered from there.

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Create a new folder for organizing apps or workflows. Specify the parent folder ID and folder type.

tools.name: rename_folder
tools.description: Rename an existing folder. Use list_apps to find folder IDs.

tools.name: delete_folder
tools.description: Permanently delete a folder. The folder must be empty (no apps or subfolders). Use list_apps to find folder IDs.

tools.name: list_resources
tools.description: List all configured resources (data sources) in the Retool organization. Resources include databases, APIs, AI providers, and other integrations.

tools.name: get_resource
tools.description: Get full details of a single resource (data source) by ID. Returns connection configuration, environment settings, and metadata. Use list_resources to find resource IDs.

tools.name: create_resource
tools.description: Create a new resource (data source) in Retool. Resources are connections to external services like REST APIs, databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL), GraphQL endpoints, and more. Once created, queries in apps can reference the resource by name.

tools.name: create_resource_folder
tools.description: Create a new folder for organizing resources (data sources). Requires a parent resource folder ID.

tools.name: delete_resource_folder
tools.description: Delete a resource folder. The folder must be empty (no resources inside).

tools.name: move_resource_to_folder
tools.description: Move a resource (data source) to a different resource folder. Use list_resources to find resource IDs.

tools.name: list_workflows
tools.description: List all workflows and workflow folders in the Retool organization. Workflows are automated processes that can be triggered by events, schedules, or webhooks.

tools.name: get_workflow
tools.description: Get the full definition of a Retool workflow including its blocks (steps), configuration, and trigger settings. Optionally specify a source control branch to view that version.

tools.name: list_workflow_runs
tools.description: List recent execution runs for a Retool workflow with pagination. Shows run status, timing, and data sizes.

tools.name: get_workflow_run
tools.description: Get detailed results for a specific workflow run, including status, timing, input/output sizes, and trigger type.

tools.name: get_workflow_run_log
tools.description: Get execution logs for a workflow run. Each log entry captures a step in the workflow execution, useful for debugging failures and understanding execution flow.

tools.name: list_workflow_triggers
tools.description: List all triggers configured for a Retool workflow. Returns both deployed (active) and latest saved (pending) triggers, including webhooks and schedules.

tools.name: get_workflow_releases
tools.description: Get the release/deployment history for a workflow. Returns an array of releases with version, deployer, and timestamps.

tools.name: get_workflow_run_count
tools.description: Get the total execution count for every workflow. Returns a map of workflow ID to run count. Useful for identifying active vs dormant workflows and monitoring workflow health.

tools.name: get_workflows_config
tools.description: Get the global workflows runtime configuration. Returns Retool backend version, code executor version, Python support, Temporal client status, and other system-level settings.

tools.name: list_environments
tools.description: List all deployment environments in the Retool organization. Environments define separate configurations for resources (e.g., production, staging).

tools.name: list_branches
tools.description: List all source control branches in the Retool organization. Branches are used for version control when source control is configured.

tools.name: get_source_control_settings
tools.description: Get the source control configuration for the Retool organization, including auto branch naming, PR templates, and branch cleanup settings.

tools.name: list_playground_queries
tools.description: List all saved playground queries for the current user and the organization. The playground allows running ad-hoc queries against connected resources.

tools.name: run_query
tools.description: Execute a SQL query against a Retool resource and return the results. Use this to test resources, inspect data, or validate queries before wiring them into an app. The resource can be specified by display name or internal UUID.

tools.name: run_grpc
tools.description: Execute a gRPC method call against a Retool gRPC resource and return the results. Use this to test gRPC resources, call service methods, or validate request/response formats. The resource can be specified by display name or internal UUID.

tools.name: list_grids
tools.description: List all Retool Database tables (grids). Retool Database is a built-in PostgreSQL database for storing app data.

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List all AI agents in the Retool organization. Agents are AI-powered assistants built within Retool.
